profile.campus: Google Central Ohio (New Albany / Columbus-Lockbourne / Lancaster), OH
profile.address: Babbitt Road, New Albany, Plain Township, Franklin County, OH 43004
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's New Albany, Ohio data center campus, mapped on Babbitt Road in Plain Township, Franklin County, and carries the informational label NBY-4 in this registry's underlying mapping data, not independently confirmed against a Google-published building index this session. Google's own Ohio locations page, fetched this session, does not name individual buildings or addresses within the campus.

Google's cloud infrastructure operates as a business of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL/GOOG, SEC CIK 0001652044), headquartered at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. Google's own Ohio data center location page, fetched fresh this session, states the company broke ground in New Albany in 2019 and has since invested more than $20 billion in the state across New Albany, Lancaster, and Columbus, generating $21.7 billion in Ohio economic activity in 2025 and contributing over $16 million in philanthropic giving since 2006.

New Albany has become the anchor of Ohio's central data center corridor since Google broke ground there in 2019, alongside major campuses for Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon Web Services, all separately tracked in this registry, though Google's own public materials describe its New Albany footprint in aggregate rather than naming individual buildings, addresses, or per-building capacity figures.

American Electric Power (AEP Ohio) is the principal electric utility serving most of the New Albany and Columbus-area data center market, and has filed with Ohio regulators for new large-load electric tariff structures in response to rapidly growing data center demand in the corridor. New Albany's community authority has used tax-increment financing agreements, and Ohio's state-level data center sales and use tax abatement program, to help anchor the cluster's continued growth alongside Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon Web Services campuses tracked elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
Google does not publish megawatt or building-specific capacity for any individual facility at its central Ohio campus. NBY-4 is one of several mapped buildings on Babbitt Road in Plain Township, Franklin County, distinguished by street coordinate and an informational label visible in mapping data but not confirmed against a Google-published building index. Google's own Ohio location page describes New Albany, Lancaster, and Columbus as a single investment footprint spanning more than $20 billion and does not name individual buildings or per-building power draw.

Central Ohio's data center corridor, anchored by New Albany since Google broke ground in 2019, now hosts large campuses for Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon Web Services as well. American Electric Power serves most of the New Albany and Columbus-area data center market and has filed with Ohio regulators for new large-load tariff structures in response to rapidly growing demand in the corridor. Tax-increment financing and Ohio's state data center sales and use tax abatement have been credited by local officials with anchoring the cluster's continued growth.

Ohio has 76 mapped data center facilities, of which 8 have published megawatt figures totaling 60.4 MW. Google's central Ohio campus is not assigned a building-specific published capacity and therefore does not rank among the state's facilities with disclosed power draw. Determining whether this particular mapped building matters to AI scaling would require a county assessor parcel lookup to establish its size, electricity connection, and use classification.
